paper_metadata.title: Quantum-Enhanced Graph Analytics: A Hybrid AI Framework for Seller Fraud Detection in Online Marketplaces

summary: The paper presents a hybrid GNN+QNN fraud-detection framework for e-commerce graphs, evaluated on an Amazon Review Graph with 3M nodes and 20M edges and a proprietary dataset with 10M transactions, 2M sellers, and 50M edges. Reported performance includes AUC 0.94 and precision@50 0.82 for the hybrid model, versus a random forest baseline AUC of 0.88; the QNN is run only on IBM Q simulated backends, with no qubit count or circuit-depth disclosure.

experiments.description: Hybrid GNN + QNN fraud-scoring experiment on e-commerce graph data, with a variational quantum neural network module evaluated in simulation and compared against classical GNN/classical ML baselines.

algorithm.variant: GNN embeddings fed into a variational QNN anomaly-scoring module
algorithm.ansatz: single-qubit rotations with entangling CNOT layers
algorithm.parameter_initialization: GNN embeddings compressed to angles via R_y(phi_j); QNN parameters not otherwise specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: GNN output embeddings h_i in R^d with d <= 4 are compressed to angles phi_j and loaded into qubits via R_y(phi_j)
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize composite loss L = L_GNN + lambda * L_QNN for seller anomaly scoring

problem_instance.description: Seller fraud detection on e-commerce graphs using Amazon Review Graph and proprietary transaction data
problem_instance.dataset_name: Amazon Review Graph; Proprietary E-Commerce Data

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic fraud clusters injected into Amazon Review Graph; proprietary multi-relational transaction graph

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Graph construction from transaction logs, review texts, device telemetry, and social signals; deduplication, normalization, entity resolution; BERT-based sentiment embeddings for reviews; dynamic snapshots over sliding windows
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare GNN variants and hybrid models against rule-based and tabular ML baselines using AUC, precision@50, recall@50, F1, and detection latency

implementation_details.classical_solver: PyTorch Geometric for GNNs; XGBoost baseline; Pennylane for QNN simulations
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature engineering from transactional, textual, and behavioral signals; graph assembly; scaling with Spark GraphX/DGL
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Gradient boosting classifier used after concatenating GNN embeddings with tabular features in one hybrid baseline

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper makes only qualitative/speculative claims about quantum-enhanced representations and does not report any asymptotic or empirical speedup for the QNN module.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not enough complexity data; the paper reports only simulated QNN runs on IBM Q backends, with no qubit count, circuit depth, or asymptotic speedup analysis.
limiting_factors: Classical baseline (random forest AUC 0.88) is close to the reported hybrid result (AUC 0.94)
The paper frames quantum benefit as speculative and low-label dependent

notes: Paper reports Pennylane for QNN simulations and IBM simulated backends, but no specific simulator device or QPU is named; hardware.type inferred as simulator_other.

No explicit qubit count, circuit depth, or parameter count is reported; only d <= 4 embedding compression and single-qubit rotations/CNOT entangling layers are described, so quantum resource fields are left null and marked inferred where applicable.
Paper makes only speculative/qualitative quantum advantage claims and does not provide asymptotic speedup analysis.
The paper reports a hybrid GNN+QNN framework with a +6% precision@50 improvement in low-label scenarios, but does not establish a practical quantum advantage or provide complexity evidence.
